title: Anthropic’s Quarterly Revenue Jumped 45% to Nearly $17 Billion
key_facts: Anthropic told investors it earned $16.8 billion in revenue in the third quarter, Business Insider has learned.
That is about 45% above the second quarter; the Wall Street Journal earlier reported about $4.8 billion for the first quarter and around $11.6 billion for the second.
Anthropic also said it reached profitability on an adjusted basis last quarter; it said this at a meeting meant to build interest in its IPO.
The company is expected to list in November at a valuation that could approach $2 trillion, which would be the largest IPO ever, according to the article.
It is unclear whether the figure counts gross or net revenue; Anthropic has historically counted gross sales through cloud partners, which it does not fully keep.
Harrison Rolfes, private company analyst at PitchBook, sees warning signs: growth is slower than before and spending is unclear.
An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment.
quote_evidence: Anthropic told investors it brought in $16.8 billion in revenue during the third quarter, Business Insider has learned.
It's unclear if the new revenue tally counts gross or net revenue, or how Anthropic arrived at its definition of profitability.
why_it_matters_hint: The first hard revenue figure from Anthropic ahead of what could be the largest stock market listing ever.
notes: WSJ original blocked; read Business Insider. FT headline says up 'nearly 50%', BI and WSJ say 45%. Valuation of 'approach $2 trillion' is BI's wording for the expected listing, not a confirmed price.
